title: The Rule for Leaving a Game
title_ja: ゲームをやめるための規則
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の人物、組織、技術の実証結果ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A voluntary activity can provide opportunities for cooperation and enjoyment precisely because its participants agree to follow a set of rules that would not necessarily apply to their ordinary lives.
sentences.ja: 任意活動は参加者が通常生活には必ずしも適用されない規則に従うことに同意するからこそ、協力と楽しみの機会を提供できる。

sentences.en: Once the activity begins, the participants may reasonably expect one another to respect the commitments that make it possible for the group to continue.
sentences.ja: 活動開始後、参加者は集団が活動を続けることを可能にする約束を互いに尊重すると合理的に期待し得る。

sentences.en: However, an agreement to participate at one point in time does not necessarily settle every question concerning a person's willingness or ability to remain involved under changed circumstances.
sentences.ja: しかしある時点での参加合意は、事情が変わったときの関与継続の意思や能力についての全問いを必ずしも解決しない。

sentences.en: The relationship between a shared commitment and the freedom to reconsider that commitment can become particularly significant when an activity depends on the participation of several individuals.
sentences.ja: 共同の約束とその約束を再考する自由の関係は、活動が複数個人の参加に依存する場合に特に重要になり得る。

sentences.en: Imagine a fictional group of students designing a cooperative game for a school event.
sentences.ja: 学校行事のため協力ゲームを設計する架空の生徒集団を想像しよう。

sentences.en: Each player is assigned a particular role, and the other players must respond to information that the person performing that role provides at different points during the game.
sentences.ja: 各プレイヤーは特定役割を割り当てられ、他プレイヤーはゲーム中の異なる時点で役割担当者が提供する情報に対応しなければならない。

sentences.en: The designers initially assume that every person who begins the game will remain involved until the group has completed its final task.
sentences.ja: 設計者は当初、ゲームを始めた全員が集団が最終課題を終えるまで関与し続けると思う。

sentences.en: One student asks what would happen if a player needed to leave before that task had been completed, perhaps because a responsibility outside the game had unexpectedly become more urgent.
sentences.ja: ある生徒はゲーム外の責任が予想外に緊急になるなどして、課題完了前にプレイヤーが退出する必要が生じたらどうなるか尋ねる。

sentences.en: The group recognizes that the difficulty concerns not only the individual player's circumstances but also the way the other players' ability to continue depends on that person's presence.
sentences.ja: 困難は個人の事情だけでなく、他プレイヤーが続けられるかがその人の存在に依存する仕方にも関わると集団は認識する。

sentences.en: One designer suggests introducing a rule that discourages players from leaving until the game ends.
sentences.ja: 一人の設計者はゲーム終了まで退出しづらくする規則を導入することを提案する。

sentences.en: Another asks whether the problem might instead be addressed by changing the arrangement through which the player's responsibilities are distributed.
sentences.ja: 別の者はプレイヤーの責任が配分される仕組みを変えることで、代わりに問題に対処できないか尋ねる。

sentences.en: For instance, the game could include a procedure through which an available participant temporarily assumes a necessary role, provided that the other players understand how the transition works.
sentences.ja: 例えば他プレイヤーが移行方法を理解しているなら、都合のつく参加者が一時的に必要役割を引き受ける手順をゲームに含められる。

sentences.en: Such an arrangement might permit a person to leave without automatically bringing the entire activity to an end, although it would introduce additional responsibilities for the people who remain.
sentences.ja: その仕組みは残る人々に追加責任を生むが、活動全体を自動的に終わらせずに退出させることができるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The group therefore needs to examine whether the procedure itself is sufficiently manageable and whether participants are informed of the possibility before they agree to join the activity.
sentences.ja: そこで手順自体が十分に扱いやすいか、参加同意前に可能性が知らされているかを集団は調べる必要がある。

sentences.en: The fictional designers distinguish an expectation that participants will communicate foreseeable changes from a requirement that they justify every decision to leave to the satisfaction of the entire group.
sentences.ja: 架空設計者は予測可能な変化を参加者が伝えるという期待と、退出判断すべてを集団全員が納得するよう正当化するという要件を区別する。

sentences.en: The first may help the group prepare for difficulties, whereas the second could place an unnecessary burden on someone whose reasons involve matters that they reasonably wish to keep private.
sentences.ja: 第一は困難への準備を助け得るが、第二は合理的に私的に保ちたい事柄が退出理由に関わる人に不要な負担を課し得る。

sentences.en: The example does not establish that one particular arrangement would be appropriate for every voluntary activity, since the consequences of leaving and the nature of the commitments involved can differ considerably.
sentences.ja: 例は退出の影響と関わる約束の性質がかなり異なり得るため、一つの仕組みが全任意活動に適切だと確定しない。

sentences.en: It does, however, suggest that the consequences of reconsidering participation depend partly on choices made by the people who design the activity.
sentences.ja: しかし参加再考の影響は活動設計者が行った選択にも依存すると示唆する。

sentences.en: An activity that respects its participants needs to consider both the expectations that enable cooperation and the practical opportunities that allow individuals to respond to changing circumstances.
sentences.ja: 参加者を尊重する活動は協力を可能にする期待と、個人が変化する事情に対応できる実際の機会の両方を考慮する必要がある。

sentences.en: These objectives need not always be treated as incompatible, particularly when the designers can reduce unnecessary dependence among participants without eliminating the value of working together.
sentences.ja: 特に設計者が協力の価値をなくさず参加者間の不要な依存を減らせるとき、これらの目標を常に両立しないと扱う必要はない。

sentences.en: Responsible design involves asking what happens when a reasonable expectation is not fulfilled rather than assuming that every participant must be able to act exactly as anticipated.
sentences.ja: 責任ある設計には全参加者が予想通りに行動できると想定せず、合理的期待が満たされない場合に何が起きるか問うことが伴う。

sentences.en: A rule for leaving a game can become as important to the quality of the shared experience as the rules for playing it.
sentences.ja: ゲームをやめるための規則は、遊ぶための規則と同じくらい共有経験の質にとって重要になり得る。

options: Cooperative commitments can matter even though participation remains subject to changing circumstances.
Every voluntary activity necessarily requires no rules.
A participant must never be expected to follow agreements.
The ability to leave automatically prevents cooperation.
questions.explanation_ja: 協力の約束と再考の自由。

options: Every player performs an identical task independently.
Players compete without any shared information.
Players have roles that supply information needed by others.
The game can only be played by one person.
questions.explanation_ja: 役割と情報の相互依存。

questions.prompt: Why does a player's early departure create a design problem?
options: Leaving always proves the player is unwilling to cooperate.
The game necessarily continues without any adjustment.
Every responsibility exists only outside the game.
The other players may depend on that person's role.

questions.prompt: What alternative to discouraging departure is proposed?
options: Force every player to continue until the event ends.
Allow another participant to temporarily assume the necessary role.
Remove all opportunities for cooperation.
Ask the absent player to complete every task remotely.
questions.explanation_ja: 役割の一時的引き継ぎ。

questions.prompt: Why must the proposed procedure still be evaluated?
options: It may add responsibilities for the remaining players.
It automatically makes every activity effortless.
It prevents participants from receiving information.
It guarantees that no one will ever leave early.
Communicating every private matter and eliminating all responsibility.
Completing the game and refusing every invitation.
Communicating foreseeable changes and proving every reason for leaving to the whole group.
Following two identical game rules.
questions.explanation_ja: 可能な事前連絡と全理由の正当化。

questions.prompt: Why might the second expectation be problematic?
options: It necessarily improves the quality of every shared experience.
It can pressure individuals to reveal private matters.
It ensures all departure reasons are understood immediately.
It removes every burden from departing players.

questions.prompt: How might design help reconcile the two objectives?
options: Assume all participants can act exactly as planned.
Require every person to share private information.
Eliminate both commitments and shared activities.
Reduce unnecessary dependence while preserving meaningful cooperation.
Difficult to explain immediately.
Already completed.
Unable to exist together.
Dependent on a schedule.

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the argument?
options: Responsible design considers how cooperative commitments and the ability to respond to changing circumstances can coexist.
Voluntary activities should require participants to stay regardless of circumstances.
Allowing anyone to leave necessarily makes cooperation impossible.
The only ethical solution is to remove all shared responsibilities.
questions.explanation_ja: 協力と状況変化への対応を両立。

paraphrases.source: However, an agreement to participate at one point in time does not necessarily settle every question concerning a person's willingness or ability to remain involved under changed circumstances.
paraphrases.rewrite: Initial consent does not resolve every question about continuing participation.

paraphrases.source: The group recognizes that the difficulty concerns not only the individual player's circumstances but also the way the other players' ability to continue depends on that person's presence.
paraphrases.rewrite: A player's departure matters because the group depends on that role.

paraphrases.source: For instance, the game could include a procedure through which an available participant temporarily assumes a necessary role, provided that the other players understand how the transition works.
paraphrases.rewrite: A role transfer could work if the remaining participants understand it.

paraphrases.source: Responsible design involves asking what happens when a reasonable expectation is not fulfilled rather than assuming that every participant must be able to act exactly as anticipated.
paraphrases.rewrite: Design should allow for unmet expectations instead of supposing every participant can follow the original plan.
